newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: GOLD PRICE FALLS AS RESERVE BANK SELLS
The revelation that the Reserve Bank of Australia has sold two thirds of its gold reserves has triggered a free-fall in the price of gold.
The Reserve Bank announced at midnight that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold over the past six months, to be re-invested in more diversified assets.
The Reserve Bank says the sales program follows the decision that the level of gold holdings, amounting to 20 per cent of its international reserves, were no longer justified.
This follows similar moves by central banks in other countries, such as the Netherlands and Canada.
The Treasurer agrees that gold no longer plays a significant role in the international financial system.
However, the announcement came as a shock to an already nervous international gold market.
After reaching a four year low yesterday, the price of gold dropped a further $9.00 overnight to $US323.65 an ounce.
ALP SET TO OPPOSE ELECTRICITY SELL-OFF IN NSW
The New South Wales ALP's powerful Administrative Committee is poised to put the brakes on the electricity sell-off debate.
The Committee, which meets this evening, is expected to tell the parliamentary wing the electricity sector has to remain in public hands.
Sources have told the ABC the Administrative Committee will agree to a motion this evening which will see it taking control of the electricity debate.
It's understood a majority of both factions will order the parliamentary wing to take no further action on the matter and will ensure the issue is sent to the party's annual conference in October.
Most party insiders believe the sale option will be easily defeated at the conference.
BEAZLEY DENIES GOING SOFT ON TARIFF REFORM
Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley has rejected a suggestion that he's going soft on tariff reform.
Former Prime Minister Gough Whitlam says any drop in the rate of tariff reduction will be to the detriment of the Labor Party.
Beazley says the issue has changed dramatically since Whitlam's days, when Ausralian industry was uncompetitive.
Beazley says careful adjustments must be made to tariffs rather than blind cuts for no good reason.
He says Australia has to make sure it doesn't move on tariffs again until it gets other countries to move on them.
Beazley says Australia has got to stop giving something for nothing, must tell the rest of the world this and get them to move on tariffs.
He says the government should not "just stupidly reduce tariffs" without addressing the real needs of Australian industry.
BEAZLEY WARNS AGAINST FLAT SALES TAX RATE
Opposition leader Kim Beazley has warned against the introduction of an across-the-board flat rate for sales tax.
The Labor Leader has responded to suggestions from the Treasurer that the tax be extended to all goods and services.
Beazley says any such move could be a GST in disguise and will shift the taxation burden unfairly on middle Australia.
He says it would also lead to a plethora of complications for small business.
Beazley says instead of the 70,000 taxation points which there are under the wholesale sales tax, there would be over a million points.
He says it's foolish to put that sort of burden on people when trying to encourage them to invest in small business and employ people.
BOAT PEOPLE SURVIVE HARSH COUNTRY IN WA
A State Emergency Service co-ordinator says a group of illegal immigrants, found in Western Australia's north yesterday, were lucky to survive in some of State's harshest country.
The 15 men, believed to be Sri Lankans aged between 18 and 42, were found just north of Coral Bay.
Police believe a Taiwanese fishing boat dropped the men off up to three days ago.
They say it could be the farthest south that such a landing has taken place.
The men spent the night at Exmouth, and will be taken to the Immigration Depatment's detention centre at Port Hedland today.
CARR TAKES TEST RIDE ON FAST TRAIN
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has been given a test ride on one of the train systems contending for the high speed Sydney to Canberra rail link.
Carr rode at 420 kilometres an hour on the magnetically-levitated Transrapid train on a test track in north Germany.
He was joined by German Government officials and Transrapid executives, who are working together to build a line from Hamburg to Berlin.
Transrapid's Australian representative Gerard Brennan says Carr indicated he was impressed by the high-tech transport system.
Brennan says everybody who has been to the test track has been very positive towards the technology, and the company believes the Transrapid system is capturing the imagination of Australia.
